correctness.rationale: Exact chord and shoelace identities give D_P=(sin a/4)sum(delta_i^2)+(cos a/24)sum(delta_i^3)+O(||delta||^4) and R=-(sin^2 a/12)sum(delta_i^3)+O(||delta||^4). Jensen localizes all near-maximal configurations. Lagrange multipliers give max absolute cubic moment (m-2)/sqrt(m(m-1)), proving the sharp coefficient with one-versus-all extremizers. The Dirichlet simplex has constant density, so after scaling the near-regular region converges to a Euclidean ball in symmetric-difference volume and hence total variation. An exact spherical sixth-moment identity yields the conditional residual variance. The standalone symbolic and numerical checker passed; finite checks supplement rather than prove the limits.

value.rationale: Area and perimeter endpoint deviations are naturally highly dependent because they share exactly the same quadratic gap energy. Their first nonproportional information is an odd cubic skewness, and the sharp upper bound identifies the maximally asymmetric near-regular geometry. The conditional law determines the full marked asymmetry distribution and a closed-form invariant for every fixed polygon order. This is not an arbitrary numerical coefficient or a marginal endpoint expansion.
